turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hello. It’s nice to meet you too. I came in today because, well, I seem to be spending far too much of my day just checking on things. 

I keep opening the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes over and over again. I just have to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are exactly where I left them. And the frustrating part is... I'll do this even when I just checked them a few minutes before. It's just taking up so much of my time and I don't know why I can't stop.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel the need to recheck those folders, drawers, or boxes, is it because you’re afraid something bad will happen if you don’t?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I wouldn't say I'm afraid of a disaster happening, no. It's more of a nagging worry. Even when I logically know better, a thought will just keep needling me that I might have accidentally thrown away my husband's old tax papers, or maybe I put a family recipe in the wrong box. 

I just can't seem to let the thought pass. If I don't go look, I just sit there feeling like I've done something terribly careless, and the only way to get rid of that feeling is to go check again.

Yes, they really do. I don't want them there at all. Like I was just saying, that... that thought about my husband's tax papers or the recipe box, it just forces its way in.
